mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a financial crisis.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 5% signals a deepening recession, causing S&P 500 20-day forward returns to be negative.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered recession episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for four consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over three consecutive months signals contraction in the manufacturing sector, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the consumer price index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary pressure, which increases risk premia and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in housing starts (HOUST) above the previous 12-month average for two consecutive months signals a recovery in the housing market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0.8%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 jobs in a single month signals a sudden labor market shock, which depresses consumer spending and corporate guidance, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls by > 100,000 in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and industrial production (INDPRO) above their 12-month moving averages signals synchronized expansion in demand and supply, which boosts earnings expectations and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 1%) in at least 60% of triggered synchronized expansion episodes.
